summary.text: Luster is the way light interacts with the surface of a crystal, rock or mineral, and the word comes from the Latin for light.
Geologists describe it with terms such as metallic, glassy, greasy, silky and earthy, and often combine them for in-between cases.
Because luster varies along a smooth range with no rigid boundaries, different sources can describe the same mineral differently.

items.prompt: A mineral is built from thin, flat, transparent sheets stacked together and splits perfectly into flakes. What luster would you expect it to show?

options.label: Metallic, like polished steel
Pearly, like the inside of a shell
Earthy, like dry clay
Adamantine, like a diamond

items.explain: Light reflecting from many thin transparent layers gives a shine reminiscent of pearls; such minerals have perfect cleavage.

items.prompt: Why does a dull, earthy mineral show little or no shine?

options.label: It contains no metal at all
Its dark color swallows the light
Coarse grains scatter light every way
It bends light far more than glass

items.explain: Coarse granulations scatter light in all directions, so no glossy reflection builds up.

items.prompt: Two field guides describe the same mineral's luster differently, one calling it glassy and the other greasy. What best explains this?

options.label: One guide used a faulty measuring instrument
Luster changes only as a mineral ages
Every mineral has one fixed luster, so one guide erred
Luster types blend with no sharp lines between them

items.explain: Luster varies over a continuum with no rigid boundaries, so sources often describe the same mineral differently.

items.prompt: A polished tiger's eye shows bright bands of light that seem to slide as you turn it. What inside the stone produces this?

options.label: Parallel fibres reflecting light sideways
A thin coating of metal on the surface
Tiny air bubbles trapped at random
Layers of differently colored glass

items.explain: Chatoyant minerals are made of parallel fibres that reflect light perpendicular to their direction, forming narrow moving bands.

items.prompt: Diamond has the most brilliant kind of luster. Which property goes along with that adamantine shine?

options.label: Perfect cleavage into thin sheets
A very high refractive index
A large amount of metal inside
Many fine fibres lined up in rows

items.explain: Adamantine minerals are transparent or translucent with a high refractive index of 1.9 or more.

items.prompt: You pick up a clear quartz crystal. Which luster term would a geologist most likely use for it?

options.label: Adamantine
Metallic
Vitreous
Waxy

items.explain: Quartz is a common example of vitreous, or glassy, luster, typical of transparent minerals with fairly low refractive indices.
